content: Ipecacuanha is an over-the-counter (OTC) emetic that has been approved by the FDA for the treatment of acute poisoning by inducing vomiting. Common adverse reactions associated with its use include diarrhea, stomach cramps, muscle pain (myalgia), and lethargy. For adults, the FDA-labeled indication for Ipecacuanha is to treat acute poisoning by inducing nausea and vomiting. The recommended dosage is to allow 3 or 4 pellets to dissolve in the mouth three times a day until symptoms are relieved or as directed by a healthcare professional. There is limited information available regarding off-label uses of Ipecacuanha in adults, whether supported by guidelines or not. For pediatric patients, the FDA-labeled indication is also for the treatment of acute poisoning. The dosage is the same as for adults: 3 or 4 pellets dissolved in the mouth three times a day until symptoms are relieved or as directed by a healthcare professional. Similarly, there is limited information on off-label uses of Ipecacuanha in pediatric patients, whether guideline-supported or not. There is limited information available regarding contraindications, warnings, and postmarketing experience for Ipecacuanha in the drug label. Adverse reactions reported in clinical trials include diarrhea, stomach cramps, myalgia, and lethargy. There is no established information on drug interactions. Regarding use in specific populations, the FDA advises consulting a healthcare professional before use if pregnant or breastfeeding. There is no specific guidance on the use of Ipecacuanha during labor and delivery, in pediatric or geriatric populations, or in relation to gender, race, renal impairment, hepatic impairment, or immunocompromised patients. Additionally, there is no guidance on its use in women of reproductive potential or in males. Ipecacuanha is administered orally. However, there is limited information on monitoring, IV compatibility, overdose, pharmacology, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, and nonclinical toxicology in the drug label. Clinical studies and details on how the drug is supplied are also not well-documented. The drug should be stored at room temperature. There is no established interaction between alcohol and Ipecacuanha, but patients are advised to consult their doctor regarding the effects of alcohol when taking this medication. The brand name for Ipecacuanha is Ipecacuanha®, and there is limited information on look-alike drug names in the drug label.
